items.text: REFERRED TO CULTURAL AFFAIRS, TOURISM, PARKS AND RECREATION

items.lawSection: Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5483

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the parks, recreation and historic
preservation law, in relation to the New York state heritage areas
advisory council

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL : increases the membership of the
New York state heritage areas advisory council from 21 to 26, and
grants council authority to elect its chair

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS : New York state heritage areas advisory
council shall consist of twenty-six members or their designated
representatives. The members of the advisory council shall elect a
chair from amongst its members for a term of three years. The heritage
areas advisory council should meet at least twice a year to provide
information and review the activities of the office of state heritage
areas.

 JUSTIFICATION : Since the NYSHAAC was created in 1982 Congress has
established 4 national heritage areas located in whole or in part in
New York State. The Erie Canalway National Heritage Corridor, for
example, is an area 540 miles in length and encompasses 11 state
heritage areas. State and national heritage areas shall similar
conservation, recreation, education and sustainable economic
development objectives. Inclusion of representatives from National
heritage areas on the advisory council will help coordinate and
maximize the positive impacts from both state and national heritage
areas. In addition, the resent establishment of the state heritage
area association as a nonprofit corporation allowing the more than 20
state heritage areas makes it timely and appropriate to include its
leader on the advisory council.

While the State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
retains various responsibilities for relating to the laws creating
state heritage areas including review of management plans, it no
longer provides day to day staffing for the state heritage area system
and primary responsibility for management of state heritage areas is
with the communities where the state heritage areas are located. Many
other state agencies like the Departments of State, Agriculture and
Markets, and Transportation and programs like I Love NY have
significant interests in the success of state and national heritage
areas. Therefore, opening up the opportunity to change the leadership
of the advisory council is an appropriate way to reflect the diversity
of representation on the advisory council.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY : New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS : None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE : This act shall take effect immediately.
